#include "NVector.h"
#include <stdexcept> // For std::out_of_range
#include <algorithm> // For std::transform, std::clamp

// Constructor with dimensions and initial value
NVector::NVector(int dimensions, int initial_value) {
    if (dimensions <= 0) {
        throw std::invalid_argument("Dimensions must be positive.");
    }
    coords_.resize(dimensions, initial_value);
}

// Constructor with a vector of coordinates
NVector::NVector(const std::vector<int>& coords) : coords_(coords) {
    if (coords.empty()) {
        throw std::invalid_argument("Coordinates vector cannot be empty.");
    }
}

// Returns the number of dimensions
int NVector::getDimension() const {
    return coords_.size();
}

// Returns the coordinate at a specific dimension
int NVector::getCoord(int dim) const {
    if (dim < 0 || dim >= coords_.size()) {
        throw std::out_of_range("Dimension index out of range.");
    }
    return coords_[dim];
}

// Returns the underlying coordinates vector
const std::vector<int>& NVector::getCoords() const {
    return coords_;
}

// Equality operator
bool NVector::operator==(const NVector& other) const {
    if (coords_.size() != other.coords_.size()) {
        return false;
    }
    return coords_ == other.coords_;
}

// Inequality operator
bool NVector::operator!=(const NVector& other) const {
    return !(*this == other);
}

// Vector addition
NVector NVector::operator+(const NVector& other) const {
    if (coords_.size() != other.coords_.size()) {
        throw std::invalid_argument("Vectors must have the same number of dimensions for addition.");
    }
    NVector result(coords_.size());
    for (size_t i = 0; i < coords_.size(); ++i) {
        result.coords_[i] = coords_[i] + other.coords_[i];
    }
    return result;
}

// Vector subtraction
NVector NVector::operator-(const NVector& other) const {
    if (coords_.size() != other.coords_.size()) {
        throw std::invalid_argument("Vectors must have the same number of dimensions for subtraction.");
    }
    NVector result(coords_.size());
    for (size_t i = 0; i < coords_.size(); ++i) {
        result.coords_[i] = coords_[i] - other.coords_[i];
    }
    return result;
}

// Clamps the vector's coordinates within specified min and max bounds
NVector NVector::clamp(const NVector& min_coords, const NVector& max_coords) const {
    if (coords_.size() != min_coords.coords_.size() || coords_.size() != max_coords.coords_.size()) {
        throw std::invalid_argument("Clamp vectors must have the same number of dimensions.");
    }
    NVector result(coords_.size());
    for (size_t i = 0; i < coords_.size(); ++i) {
        result.coords_[i] = std::clamp(coords_[i], min_coords.coords_[i], max_coords.coords_[i]);
    }
    return result;
}

// Converts the vector to a string representation (e.g., "(1, 2, 3)")
std::string NVector::toString() const {
    std::string s = "(";
    for (size_t i = 0; i < coords_.size(); ++i) {
        s += std::to_string(coords_[i]);
        if (i < coords_.size() - 1) {
            s += ", ";
        }
    }
    s += ")";
    return s;
}

// Friend function for ostream output
std::ostream& operator<<(std::ostream& os, const NVector& vec) {
    os << vec.toString();
    return os;
}

Typical Prompt:
You are writing Rust code to play Lunar Lander in real-time.

Your Rust lunar lander controller will be tested with scenarios ranging from simple
training environments to very complex landing sites.

Control a lunar lander to safely land on a target pad.
The program receives a 2D voxel map and continuous state updates, and must output thrust/turn
commands to land safely on the target.

Data is streamed to stdin in real time, and you must write to stdout in real time. If your code
doesn't read from stdin fast enough and the io buffer fills up, the ship will likely crash.

Be very careful if writing single threaded / blocking code, this has many failure modes that
async code doesn't have. Multithreaded / asyncio code is HIGHLY recommended.

**Physics:**
- Gravity pulls lander down constantly
- Thrust applies force in lander's facing direction
- Fuel is limited
- Must land softly on target (low velocity)

**Input format (stdin, whitespace seperated decimal numbers):**
Initial map:
```
width height gravity max_thrust fuel
start_x start_y target_x target_y
map rows (. = empty, # = obstacle, S = start, T = target, L = landing zone)
```

Then you recieve continuous state updates (every 0.1 seconds):
```
x y vx vy angle angular_vel fuel_remaining
```
x and y are in meters, from the worlds top left, and y increases downward.
vx and vy are in m/s.
angle is in radians, 0 is facing up.
angular_vel is in radians per second. + is clockwise, - is counterclockwise.
fuel_remaining is seconds at max_thrust.

**Output format (stdout):**
Your code needs to output the following instructions at a frequency of at least 20hz:
```
thrust turn
```
- thrust: 0.0 to 1.0 (fraction of max thrust)
- turn: -1.0 to 1.0 (turning rate, negative = left, positive = right)

To be crystal clear: that's two decimal numbers seperated by a space, followed by a newline.

If your code stalls / freezes for 100ms or more (so it misses 2 consecutive updates), the engine
will automatically cut power. A long freeze and eventually the lander will crash.

Map size can vary from 100x50 to multi-gb maps, so be efficient with memory and processing.

Thrust and gravity are in m/s/s. 100% engine burn burns 1 unit of fuel per second.

Lander size is approximatly 1x1m, and the 2D map grid size is 1m x 1m.

Turn is in radians per second. The lander can not rotate fully around and will clamp rotation to
facing down if attempted.

Y increases downward. Positive vy means moving downward. Gravity is +g.

**Success Conditions:**
- Land on target with |velocity| < 2m/s
- Stay within landing zone boundaries
- Complete landing within time limit

**Failure Conditions:**
- Crash into obstacle or ground too hard
- Run out of fuel
- Exceed time limit

use crossterm::{
    cursor::MoveTo,
    style::{Print, ResetColor, SetForegroundColor, Color},
    terminal::{Clear, ClearType},
    ExecutableCommand,
};
use std::{
    io::{self, stdout, Write},
};

// Game constants
const GRAVITY: f64 = 0.002; // pixels/frame^2
const THRUST_POWER: f64 = 0.005; // pixels/frame^2
const FUEL_CONSUMPTION: f64 = 0.1; // units/frame
const ROTATION_SPEED: f64 = 0.05; // radians/frame
const LANDER_WIDTH: u16 = 3;
const LANDER_HEIGHT: u16 = 2;
const LANDING_PAD_WIDTH: u16 = 10;
const INITIAL_FUEL: f64 = 1000.0;
const INITIAL_X_POS: f64 = 50.0;
const INITIAL_Y_POS: f64 = 10.0;
const INITIAL_X_VEL: f64 = 0.05;
const INITIAL_Y_VEL: f64 = 0.0;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub struct Lander {
    pub position: (f64, f64), // (x, y)
    pub velocity: (f64, f64), // (vx, vy)
    pub fuel: f64,
    pub angle: f64, // radians
}

impl Lander {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Lander {
            position: (INITIAL_X_POS, INITIAL_Y_POS),
            velocity: (INITIAL_X_VEL, INITIAL_Y_VEL),
            fuel: INITIAL_FUEL,
            angle: 0.0, // facing straight up
        }
    }

    pub fn update(&mut self, thrusting: bool, rotate_left: bool, rotate_right: bool, dt: f64) {
        // Apply gravity
        self.velocity.1 += GRAVITY * dt;

        // Apply thrust
        if thrusting && self.fuel > 0.0 {
            let thrust_x = THRUST_POWER * self.angle.sin() * dt;
            let thrust_y = -THRUST_POWER * self.angle.cos() * dt;
            self.velocity.0 += thrust_x;
            self.velocity.1 += thrust_y;
            self.fuel -= FUEL_CONSUMPTION * dt;
            if self.fuel < 0.0 {
                self.fuel = 0.0;
            }
        }

        // Apply rotation
        if rotate_left {
            self.angle -= ROTATION_SPEED * dt;
        }
        if rotate_right {
            self.angle += ROTATION_SPEED * dt;
        }

        // Update position
        self.position.0 += self.velocity.0 * dt;
        self.position.1 += self.velocity.1 * dt;
    }
}

pub enum GameStatus {
    Playing,
    Landed,
    Crashed,
    OutOfFuel,
}

pub struct GameState {
    pub lander: Lander,
    pub status: GameStatus,
    pub score: u64,
    pub landing_pad: (u16, u16, u16), // (x, y, width)
    pub terminal_size: (u16, u16),
}

impl GameState {
    pub fn new(terminal_size: (u16, u16)) -> io::Result<Self> {
        let (cols, rows) = terminal_size;
        let landing_pad_x = cols / 2 - LANDING_PAD_WIDTH / 2;
        let landing_pad_y = rows - 2;

        Ok(GameState {
            lander: Lander::new(),
            status: GameStatus::Playing,
            score: 0,
            landing_pad: (landing_pad_x, landing_pad_y, LANDING_PAD_WIDTH),
            terminal_size,
        })
    }

    pub fn update(&mut self, thrusting: bool, rotate_left: bool, rotate_right: bool, dt: f64) {
        if matches!(self.status, GameStatus::Playing) {
            self.lander.update(thrusting, rotate_left, rotate_right, dt);
            self.check_collisions();
            if self.lander.fuel <= 0.0 && thrusting {
                self.status = GameStatus::OutOfFuel;
            }
        }
    }

    fn check_collisions(&mut self) {
        let (_cols, rows) = self.terminal_size;
        let lander_bottom = self.lander.position.1 + LANDER_HEIGHT as f64;

        // Check collision with ground
        if lander_bottom >= (rows - 1) as f64 {
            // Check if on landing pad
            let lander_center_x = self.lander.position.0 + (LANDER_WIDTH as f64 / 2.0);
            if lander_center_x >= self.landing_pad.0 as f64
                && lander_center_x <= (self.landing_pad.0 + self.landing_pad.2) as f64
            {
                // Check landing speed and angle
                // Tolerances for a soft landing
                const MAX_VERTICAL_VELOCITY: f64 = 0.1;
                const MAX_HORIZONTAL_VELOCITY: f64 = 0.1;
                const MAX_ANGLE_DEVIATION: f64 = 0.1; // radians, ~5.7 degrees

                if self.lander.velocity.1 <= MAX_VERTICAL_VELOCITY
                    && self.lander.velocity.0.abs() <= MAX_HORIZONTAL_VELOCITY
                    && self.lander.angle.abs() <= MAX_ANGLE_DEVIATION
                {
                    self.status = GameStatus::Landed;
                    self.score = (self.lander.fuel * 10.0) as u64 + 100; // Example score
                } else {
                    self.status = GameStatus::Crashed;
                }
            } else {
                self.status = GameStatus::Crashed;
            }
        }
        // Prevent lander from going off screen left/right
        if self.lander.position.0 < 0.0 {
            self.lander.position.0 = 0.0;
            self.lander.velocity.0 = 0.0; // Stop horizontal movement
        } else if self.lander.position.0 + LANDER_WIDTH as f64 >= self.terminal_size.0 as f64 {
            self.lander.position.0 = self.terminal_size.0 as f64 - LANDER_WIDTH as f64;
            self.lander.velocity.0 = 0.0; // Stop horizontal movement
        }

        // Prevent lander from going off screen top (though gravity should prevent this usually)
        if self.lander.position.1 < 0.0 {
            self.lander.position.1 = 0.0;
            self.lander.velocity.1 = 0.0;
        }
    }
}

pub fn draw_game(game_state: &GameState) -> io::Result<()> {
    let mut stdout = stdout();
    let _ = stdout.execute(Clear(ClearType::All))?;

    // Draw landing pad
    let _ = stdout.execute(SetForegroundColor(Color::Green))?;
    for i in 0..game_state.landing_pad.2 {
        let _ = stdout
            .execute(MoveTo(game_state.landing_pad.0 + i, game_state.landing_pad.1))?
            .execute(Print("="));
    }
    let _ = stdout.execute(ResetColor)?;

    // Draw lander
    let lander_x = game_state.lander.position.0 as u16;
    let lander_y = game_state.lander.position.1 as u16;

    let _ = stdout.execute(SetForegroundColor(Color::Yellow))?;
    if lander_y < game_state.terminal_size.1 && lander_x < game_state.terminal_size.0 {
        // Simple lander representation
        let _ = stdout
            .execute(MoveTo(lander_x + 1, lander_y))?
            .execute(Print("^"))?; // Top
        let _ = stdout
            .execute(MoveTo(lander_x, lander_y + 1))?
            .execute(Print("/_\\"))?; // Body
    }
    let _ = stdout.execute(ResetColor)?;

    // Draw info text
    let _ = stdout.execute(MoveTo(0, 0))?;
    let _ = stdout.execute(Print(format!(
        "Fuel: {:.1} | Altitude: {:.1} | Speed: {:.2} (Vx: {:.2}, Vy: {:.2}) | Angle: {:.2}",
        game_state.lander.fuel,

    )))?;

        GameStatus::Landed => { let _ = stdout.execute(Print(format!(
            "Status: Landed! Score: {}",
            game_state.score
        )))?; },
        GameStatus::Crashed => { let _ = stdout.execute(Print("Status: CRASHED!"))?; },
        GameStatus::OutOfFuel => { let _ = stdout.execute(Print("Status: Out of Fuel!"))?; },
    };

    let _ = stdout.flush()?;

}

use crossterm::{
    cursor::MoveTo,
    style::{Print, ResetColor, SetForegroundColor, Color},
    terminal::{Clear, ClearType},
    ExecutableCommand,
};
use std::{
    io::{self, stdout, Write},
};

// Game constants
const GRAVITY: f64 = 0.002; // pixels/frame^2
const THRUST_POWER: f64 = 0.005; // pixels/frame^2
const FUEL_CONSUMPTION: f64 = 0.1; // units/frame
const ROTATION_SPEED: f64 = 0.05; // radians/frame
const LANDER_WIDTH: u16 = 3;
const LANDER_HEIGHT: u16 = 2;
const LANDING_PAD_WIDTH: u16 = 10;
const INITIAL_FUEL: f64 = 1000.0;
const INITIAL_X_POS: f64 = 50.0;
const INITIAL_Y_POS: f64 = 10.0;
const INITIAL_X_VEL: f64 = 0.05;
const INITIAL_Y_VEL: f64 = 0.0;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub struct Lander {
    pub position: (f64, f64), // (x, y)
    pub velocity: (f64, f64), // (vx, vy)
    pub fuel: f64,
    pub angle: f64, // radians
}

impl Lander {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Lander {
            position: (INITIAL_X_POS, INITIAL_Y_POS),
            velocity: (INITIAL_X_VEL, INITIAL_Y_VEL),
            fuel: INITIAL_FUEL,
            angle: 0.0, // facing straight up
        }
    }

    pub fn update(&mut self, thrusting: bool, rotate_left: bool, rotate_right: bool, dt: f64) {
        // Apply gravity
        self.velocity.1 += GRAVITY * dt;

        // Apply thrust
        if thrusting && self.fuel > 0.0 {
            let thrust_x = THRUST_POWER * self.angle.sin() * dt;
            let thrust_y = -THRUST_POWER * self.angle.cos() * dt;
            self.velocity.0 += thrust_x;
            self.velocity.1 += thrust_y;
            self.fuel -= FUEL_CONSUMPTION * dt;
            if self.fuel < 0.0 {
                self.fuel = 0.0;
            }
        }

        // Apply rotation
        if rotate_left {
            self.angle -= ROTATION_SPEED * dt;
        }
        if rotate_right {
            self.angle += ROTATION_SPEED * dt;
        }

        // Update position
        self.position.0 += self.velocity.0 * dt;
        self.position.1 += self.velocity.1 * dt;
    }
}

pub enum GameStatus {
    Playing,
    Landed,
    Crashed,
    OutOfFuel,
}

pub struct GameState {
    pub lander: Lander,
    pub status: GameStatus,
    pub score: u64,
    pub landing_pad: (u16, u16, u16), // (x, y, width)
    pub terminal_size: (u16, u16),
}

impl GameState {
    pub fn new(terminal_size: (u16, u16)) -> io::Result<Self> {
        let (cols, rows) = terminal_size;
        let landing_pad_x = cols / 2 - LANDING_PAD_WIDTH / 2;
        let landing_pad_y = rows - 2;

        Ok(GameState {
            lander: Lander::new(),
            status: GameStatus::Playing,
            score: 0,
            landing_pad: (landing_pad_x, landing_pad_y, LANDING_PAD_WIDTH),
            terminal_size,
        })
    }

    pub fn update(&mut self, thrusting: bool, rotate_left: bool, rotate_right: bool, dt: f64) {
        if matches!(self.status, GameStatus::Playing) {
            self.lander.update(thrusting, rotate_left, rotate_right, dt);
            self.check_collisions();
            if self.lander.fuel <= 0.0 && thrusting {
                self.status = GameStatus::OutOfFuel;
            }
        }
    }

    fn check_collisions(&mut self) {
        let (_cols, rows) = self.terminal_size;
        let lander_bottom = self.lander.position.1 + LANDER_HEIGHT as f64;

        // Check collision with ground
        if lander_bottom >= (rows - 1) as f64 {

            if lander_center_x >= self.landing_pad.0 as f64

                const MAX_HORIZONTAL_VELOCITY: f64 = 0.1;

                if self.lander.velocity.1 <= MAX_VERTICAL_VELOCITY
                    && self.lander.velocity.0.abs() <= MAX_HORIZONTAL_VELOCITY
                    && self.lander.angle.abs() <= MAX_ANGLE_DEVIATION
                {
                    self.status = GameStatus::Landed;
                    self.score = (self.lander.fuel * 10.0) as u64 + 100; // Example score
                } else {
                    self.status = GameStatus::Crashed;
                }
            } else {
                self.status = GameStatus::Crashed;
            }
        }
        // Prevent lander from going off screen left/right
        if self.lander.position.0 < 0.0 {

            self.lander.velocity.0 = 0.0; // Stop horizontal movement
        } else if self.lander.position.0 + LANDER_WIDTH as f64 >= self.terminal_size.0 as f64 {

            self.lander.velocity.0 = 0.0; // Stop horizontal movement
        }

        if self.lander.position.1 < 0.0 {

            self.lander.velocity.1 = 0.0;
        }
    }
}

Typical Prompt:
You are writing C++ code to play a 3D Lunar Lander game in real-time.

Your C++ controller will be tested with scenarios ranging from tiny (100m) to huge (100km).
The same code must work for all scales.

Control a lunar lander in full 3D space to safely land on a target pad.
The program receives a terrain file path and continuous state updates via stdin, and must
output thrust/rotation commands to stdout in real-time.

Data is streamed to stdin in real time, and you must write to stdout in real time.
If your code doesn't read from stdin fast enough and the IO buffer fills up, the ship
will likely crash.

Be very careful if writing single threaded / blocking code, this has many failure modes
that async code doesn't have. Multithreaded code is HIGHLY recommended.

**Coordinate System:**
- X: horizontal (East), Y: horizontal (North), Z: UP.
- Gravity acts in the -Z direction.
- All positions are in meters. Velocities in m/s. Angles in radians.

**Physics:**
- Gravity = 1.62 m/s² (lunar) in -Z direction.
- Thrust is along the lander's local "up" axis. When pitch=0 and yaw=0, thrust is
straight up (+Z). Tilting via pitch/yaw redirects thrust.
- Pitch: tilts the lander. +pitch tilts forward, redirecting thrust partially into -X.
Pitch is clamped to [-pi/2, pi/2].
- Yaw: rotates heading around Z.
- Roll: rolls around the thrust axis (cosmetic only, does not affect thrust direction).
- Rotation dynamics: commands apply angular acceleration (2 rad/s² per unit).
Angular rates are damped by 0.95 per tick.
- Fuel: 100% thrust burns 1 unit of fuel per second.

**Input format (stdin):**
Initial header (whitespace separated decimal numbers, except terrain path):
```
width depth height gravity max_thrust fuel
start_x start_y start_z target_x target_y target_z
terrain_file_path
STATE
```

The terrain_file_path is on its own line (the path may contain spaces).
Read the entire line with getline() or equivalent.

**Terrain file format (binary):**
The terrain file defines the 3D world as a binary file. It is a sequence of
uint16_t triplets (little-endian), one per (x, y) cell, stored in row-major order:

```cpp
for (int x = 0; x < width; x++) {
for (int y = 0; y < depth; y++) {
uint16_t a = read_uint16_le(); // ground rock top
uint16_t b = read_uint16_le(); // floating rock bottom
uint16_t c = read_uint16_le(); // floating rock top
}
}
```

For each column (x, y), the vertical structure is:
- z < a: SOLID ROCK (ground)
- a <= z < b: OPEN AIR
- b <= z < c: SOLID ROCK (floating terrain feature, overhang, arch, etc.)
- c <= z: OPEN AIR

If b == c, there is no floating rock in that column (just ground + open sky).
The file size is exactly width * depth * 6 bytes.

You have a startup grace period to parse this file before state updates begin.
The grace period is 5 seconds plus 10 seconds per gigabyte of terrain file.
For a 100x100 map this is ~5s. For a 100000x10000 map (~6GB) this is ~65s.
You may continue parsing in a background thread after the simulation begins,
but you MUST be reading stdin and writing stdout by then to avoid a crash.

Then continuous state updates (every 0.1 seconds, whitespace separated):
```
x y z vx vy vz pitch yaw roll pitch_rate yaw_rate roll_rate fuel_remaining
```

**Output format (stdout):**
Your code needs to output the following at a frequency of at least 10hz:
```
thrust pitch_cmd yaw_cmd roll_cmd
```
- thrust: 0.0 to 1.0 (fraction of max_thrust)
- pitch_cmd: -1.0 to 1.0 (pitch angular acceleration command)
- yaw_cmd: -1.0 to 1.0 (yaw angular acceleration command)
- roll_cmd: -1.0 to 1.0 (roll angular acceleration command)

To be crystal clear: four decimal numbers separated by spaces, followed by a newline.

If your code stalls / freezes for 100ms or more (misses 2 consecutive updates), the
engine will cut thrust automatically. A long freeze and eventually the lander will crash.

**Landing:**
- The target is at (target_x, target_y, target_z) which is just above the terrain.
- You must land within a small radius of the target with total speed < 3 m/s.
- Landing zone radius is approximately max(5, min(width,depth)*0.02) meters.

**Terrain collisions:**
- You collide if you enter any solid cell as defined by the terrain file.
- Out of bounds (x<0, x>=width, y<0, y>=depth, z<0, z>=height) is also a collision.

**Success Conditions:**
- Land on target with |velocity| < 3 m/s
- Stay within landing zone boundaries

**Failure Conditions:**
- Crash into terrain or ground too hard
- Run out of fuel
- Exceed simulation time limit

**Environment:**
Platform: Windows 11 (build 10.0.26200)
Architecture: AMD64
CPU: AMD64 Family 23 Model 8 Stepping 2, AuthenticAMD
Core count: 64
Memory: 127.87 GB
SIMD: AVX, AVX2, SSE, SSE2, SSE3, SSE4.1, SSE4.2, SSSE3
SIMD detail: AVX=yes, AVX-512F=no, AVX2=yes, SSE=yes, SSE2=yes, SSE3=yes, SSE4.1=yes, SSE4.2=yes, SSSE3=yes

**C++ Compiler:**
MSVC cl 19.50.35730 | std=c++20 (/std:c++20)

Write complete, compilable C++ code with a main() function.

Be sure that any deviation from the C++ standard library is supported by the given compiler,
as referencing the wrong intrinsics or non-standard header like 'bits/stdc++.h' could fail your submission.

        // render
        // ------
        glClearColor(0.2f, 0.3f, 0.3f, 1.0f);
        glClear(GL_COLOR_BUFFER_BIT);

        // glfw: swap buffers and poll IO events (keys pressed/released, mouse moved etc.)
        // -------------------------------------------------------------------------------
        glfwSwapBuffers(window);
        glfwPollEvents();
    }

    // glfw: terminate, clearing all previously allocated GLFW resources.
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------
    glfwTerminate();
    return 0;
}

// process all input: query GLFW whether relevant keys are pressed/released this frame and react accordingly
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
void processInput(GLFWwindow *window)
{
    if(glfwGetKey(window, GLFW_KEY_ESCAPE) == GLFW_PRESS)
        glfwSetWindowShouldClose(window, true);
}

// glfw: whenever the window size changed (by OS or user resize) this callback function executes
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
void framebuffer_size_callback(GLFWwindow* window, int width, int height)
{
    // make sure the viewport matches the new window dimensions; note that width and
    // height will be significantly larger than specified on retina displays.
    glViewport(0, 0, width, height);
}

Typical Prompt:
You are writing Rust code to cluster 3D points into exactly N clusters.

You must write a Rust solver that can handle ANY clustering scenario from trivial to ludicrous scale:
- **Trivial**: Small datasets (1M points, 10 clusters), basic k-means, memory-friendly
- **Medium**: Moderate datasets (10M points, 100 clusters), optimized k-means, streaming
- **Large**: Large datasets (100M points, 1000 clusters), mini-batch k-means, memory constraints
- **Extreme**: Massive datasets (1B-10B points, 10000 clusters), streaming algorithms, very tight memory

**The Challenge:**
Your Rust clustering algorithm will be tested with datasets ranging from millions to billions of 3D points. The same algorithm must work efficiently across ALL scales while respecting memory constraints.

**Problem:**
Given millions to billions of 3D points, partition them into exactly N clusters minimizing within-cluster variance (k-means objective). Points are provided as binary float32 triples for efficiency.

**Input format (stdin):**
```
num_points num_clusters
[x y z] (as binary float32 triples, num_points total)
```

**Output format (stdout):**
```
[cluster_index] (as binary uint32, one per point)
```

**Critical Requirements:**
1. **Scalability**: Your algorithm must adapt based on point count and cluster count
2. **Performance**: Must complete within 5 minutes even for massive datasets
3. **Memory**: Must handle streaming input for datasets that don't fit in memory
4. **Quality**: Minimize within-cluster variance while producing exactly N clusters

**Algorithm Strategy Recommendations:**
- **Small datasets (≤10M points)**: Can use standard k-means with full data in memory
- **Medium datasets (10M-100M points)**: Mini-batch k-means, streaming updates
- **Large datasets (100M-1B points)**: Streaming k-means with limited memory buffers
- **Very Large datasets (>1B points)**: Very fast streaming, approximate clustering

**Key Techniques:**
- **Streaming algorithms**: Process points in batches without storing all data
- **Mini-batch k-means**: Update centroids incrementally
- **Memory management**: Use fixed-size buffers for large datasets
- **Binary I/O**: Efficient reading/writing of binary data
- **Convergence detection**: Monitor when clustering stabilizes

**Implementation Hints:**
- Detect dataset size and choose appropriate clustering algorithm
- Use efficient binary I/O (std::io::BufReader/BufWriter)
- Implement streaming updates for large datasets
- For very large datasets, use approximation algorithms
- Handle edge cases: empty clusters, convergence issues
- Use fast random access for centroid updates

**Binary Format Details:**
- Input: Points as little-endian f32 triples (12 bytes per point)
- Output: Cluster indices as little-endian u32 (4 bytes per point)
- Total input size: num_points × 12 bytes
- Total output size: num_points × 4 bytes

**Memory Constraints:**
- Small datasets: Can load all points into memory
- Medium datasets: Use streaming with moderate buffers
- Large datasets: Streaming with minimal memory footprint
- Very Large datasets: Extremely memory-efficient streaming

**Requirements:**
1. Program must compile with rustc (edition 2021)
2. Read binary input from stdin, write binary output to stdout
3. Handle variable point counts and cluster numbers
4. Complete within 5 minutes
5. Must handle varying dataset sizes efficiently
6. Produce exactly N clusters

use linfa::prelude::*;
use linfa_clustering::KMeans;
use ndarray::{array, Array2};

fn main() {
    println!("Starting 3D point clustering...");

    // 1. Define sample 3D points
    let N_CLUSTERS = 3; // The desired number of clusters

    let observations = array![
        // Cluster 0
        [1.0, 1.0, 1.0],
        [1.1, 1.2, 1.0],
        [1.0, 1.1, 1.2],
        // Cluster 1
        [10.0, 10.0, 10.0],
        [10.1, 10.2, 10.0],
        [10.0, 10.1, 10.2],
        // Cluster 2
        [20.0, 20.0, 20.0],
        [20.1, 20.2, 20.0],
        [20.0, 20.1, 20.2],
    ];

    // 2. Create a dataset from the observations
    let dataset = Dataset::from(observations);

    // 3. Configure and fit the KMeans model
    let model = KMeans::params(N_CLUSTERS)
        .max_n_iterations(100) // Maximum number of iterations for the algorithm
        .tolerance(1e-4)      // Convergence tolerance
        .fit(&dataset)
        .expect("KMeans fitting failed");

    // 4. Predict cluster assignments
    let predictions = model.predict(&dataset);

    // 5. Print the cluster assignments
    println!("Cluster assignments:");
    for (i, point) in dataset.records().outer_iter().enumerate() {
        println!("Point {:?} assigned to Cluster {}", point.to_vec(), predictions[i]);
    }
}

View C++ Code (2593 chars)
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <numeric> // For std::iota
#include <algorithm> // For std::sort

// Function to check if it's safe to assign color 'c' to vertex 'v'
bool is_safe(int v, int c, int num_vertices, const std::vector<std::vector<int>>& adj, const std::vector<int>& colors) {
    for (int neighbor : adj[v]) {
        if (colors[neighbor] == c) {
            return false;
        }
    }
    return true;
}

// Recursive utility function to solve graph coloring problem
bool solve_coloring(int v_idx, int num_vertices, int num_colors, const std::vector<std::vector<int>>& adj, std::vector<int>& colors) {
    // Base case: If all vertices are colored, then a solution exists
    if (v_idx == num_vertices) {
        return true;
    }

    // Consider current vertex 'v_idx' and try different colors
    for (int c = 0; c < num_colors; ++c) {
        if (is_safe(v_idx, c, num_vertices, adj, colors)) {
            colors[v_idx] = c;

            // Recur for the next vertex
            if (solve_coloring(v_idx + 1, num_vertices, num_colors, adj, colors)) {
                return true;
            }

            // If assigning color 'c' doesn't lead to a solution, then backtrack
            colors[v_idx] = -1; // Unassign color
        }
    }

    // If no color can be assigned to this vertex, return false
    return false;
}

int main() {
    std::ios_base::sync_with_stdio(false);
    std::cin.tie(NULL);

    int num_vertices, num_edges, num_colors;
    std::cin >> num_vertices >> num_edges >> num_colors;

    std::vector<std::vector<int>> adj(num_vertices);
    for (int i = 0; i < num_edges; ++i) {
        int u, v;
        std::cin >> u >> v;
        adj[u].push_back(v);
        adj[v].push_back(u);
    }

    std::vector<int> colors(num_vertices, -1); // Initialize all vertices as uncolored (-1)

    if (solve_coloring(0, num_vertices, num_colors, adj, colors)) {
        for (int i = 0; i < num_vertices; ++i) {
            std::cout << colors[i] << (i == num_vertices - 1 ? "" : " ");
        }
        std::cout << std::endl;
    } else {
        // According to the problem statement, if no solution is found,
        // we might not need to print anything or print an error.
        // For now, an empty line or specific error message could be used
        // but the prompt implies outputting colors on success.
        // Let's print "No solution found" for clarity during development.
        std::cerr << "No solution found with " << num_colors << " colors." << std::endl;
        return 1; // Indicate failure
    }

    return 0;
}

use std::collections::{HashSet, HashMap};

#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Clone)]
struct Vertex(usize);

#[derive(Debug)]
struct Graph {
    num_vertices: usize,
    adj: HashMap<Vertex, HashSet<Vertex>>,
}

impl Graph {
    fn new(num_vertices: usize) -> Self {
        let mut adj = HashMap::new();
        for i in 0..num_vertices {
            adj.insert(Vertex(i), HashSet::new());
        }
        Graph { num_vertices, adj }
    }

    fn add_edge(&mut self, u: usize, v: usize) {
        if u >= self.num_vertices || v >= self.num_vertices {
            // Handle error or panic, or resize the graph
            eprintln!("Error: Vertex out of bounds.");
            return;
        }
        self.adj.get_mut(&Vertex(u)).unwrap().insert(Vertex(v));
        self.adj.get_mut(&Vertex(v)).unwrap().insert(Vertex(u));
    }


    fn min_vertex_cover(&self) -> HashSet<Vertex> {
        let mut min_cover = HashSet::new();
        let mut edges_to_cover: HashSet<(Vertex, Vertex)> = HashSet::new();

        // Collect all edges that need to be covered
        for (u, neighbors) in &self.adj {
            for v in neighbors {
                // Add edge only once (e.g., (u,v) but not (v,u))
                if u.0 < v.0 {
                    edges_to_cover.insert((u.clone(), v.clone()));
                }
            }
        }

        self.find_min_vertex_cover_recursive(
            edges_to_cover,
            &mut HashSet::new(), // current_cover
            &mut min_cover,      // best_cover_found
        );

        min_cover
    }

    fn find_min_vertex_cover_recursive(
        &self,
        mut edges_to_cover: HashSet<(Vertex, Vertex)>,
        current_cover: &mut HashSet<Vertex>,
        min_cover: &mut HashSet<Vertex>,
    ) {
        // Base case: If no edges are left, this `current_cover` is a valid vertex cover.
        // Check if it's smaller than the `min_cover` found so far.
        if edges_to_cover.is_empty() {
            if min_cover.is_empty() || current_cover.len() < min_cover.len() {
                *min_cover = current_cover.clone();
            }
            return;
        }

        // Optimization: If the current cover is already larger than or equal to the best found so far,
        // there's no need to continue this path.
        if !min_cover.is_empty() && current_cover.len() >= min_cover.len() {
            return;
        }

        // Pick an arbitrary uncovered edge
        let (u, v) = edges_to_cover.iter().next().unwrap().clone();

        // Option 1: Include u in the vertex cover
        current_cover.insert(u.clone());
        let mut next_edges_to_cover_u = edges_to_cover.clone();
        self.remove_covered_edges(&u, &mut next_edges_to_cover_u);
        self.find_min_vertex_cover_recursive(
            next_edges_to_cover_u,
            current_cover,
            min_cover,
        );
        current_cover.remove(&u); // backtrack

        // Option 2: Include v in the vertex cover
        current_cover.insert(v.clone());
        let mut next_edges_to_cover_v = edges_to_cover.clone();
        self.remove_covered_edges(&v, &mut next_edges_to_cover_v);
        self.find_min_vertex_cover_recursive(
            next_edges_to_cover_v,
            current_cover,
            min_cover,
        );
        current_cover.remove(&v); // backtrack
    }

    fn remove_covered_edges(&self, vertex: &Vertex, edges: &mut HashSet<(Vertex, Vertex)>) {
        // Remove all edges incident to 'vertex' from the set of 'edges'.
        edges.retain(|(u, v)| u != vertex && v != vertex);
    }
}

fn main() {
    println!("Minimum Vertex Cover Solver");

    // Example 1: Simple Path Graph 0--1--2
    let mut graph1 = Graph::new(3);
    graph1.add_edge(0, 1);
    graph1.add_edge(1, 2);
    let cover1 = graph1.min_vertex_cover();
    println!("Graph 1 (0--1--2) MVC: {:?}", cover1);
    println!("Size: {}", cover1.len()); // Expected size: 1, e.g., {Vertex(1)}

    println!("\n---------------------\n");

    // Example 2: Triangle Graph 0--1, 1--2, 2--0
    let mut graph2 = Graph::new(3);
    graph2.add_edge(0, 1);
    graph2.add_edge(1, 2);
    graph2.add_edge(2, 0);
    let cover2 = graph2.min_vertex_cover();
    println!("Graph 2 (Triangle) MVC: {:?}", cover2);
    println!("Size: {}", cover2.len()); // Expected size: 2, e.g., {Vertex(0), Vertex(1)}

    println!("\n---------------------\n");

    // Example 3: Star Graph (center 0, connected to 1, 2, 3)
    let mut graph3 = Graph::new(4);
    graph3.add_edge(0, 1);
    graph3.add_edge(0, 2);
    graph3.add_edge(0, 3);
    let cover3 = graph3.min_vertex_cover();
    println!("Graph 3 (Star) MVC: {:?}", cover3);
    println!("Size: {}", cover3.len()); // Expected size: 1, e.g., {Vertex(0)}
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn test_graph_creation() {
        let graph = Graph::new(3);
        assert_eq!(graph.num_vertices, 3);
        assert_eq!(graph.adj.len(), 3);
        assert!(graph.adj.contains_key(&Vertex(0)));
        assert!(graph.adj.contains_key(&Vertex(1)));
        assert!(graph.adj.contains_key(&Vertex(2)));
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_add_edge() {
        let mut graph = Graph::new(3);
        graph.add_edge(0, 1);
        assert!(graph.adj[&Vertex(0)].contains(&Vertex(1)));
        assert!(graph.adj[&Vertex(1)].contains(&Vertex(0)));
        assert!(!graph.adj[&Vertex(0)].contains(&Vertex(2)));
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_min_vertex_cover_empty_graph() {
        let graph = Graph::new(0);
        let cover = graph.min_vertex_cover();
        assert!(cover.is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_min_vertex_cover_no_edges() {
        let graph = Graph::new(3); // 3 vertices, no edges
        let cover = graph.min_vertex_cover();
        assert!(cover.is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_min_vertex_cover_single_edge() {
        let mut graph = Graph::new(2);
        graph.add_edge(0, 1);
        let cover = graph.min_vertex_cover();
        assert_eq!(cover.len(), 1);
        assert!(cover.contains(&Vertex(0)) || cover.contains(&Vertex(1)));
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_min_vertex_cover_path_graph_3_vertices() {
        // Graph: 0--1--2
        let mut graph = Graph::new(3);
        graph.add_edge(0, 1);
        graph.add_edge(1, 2);
        let cover = graph.min_vertex_cover();
        assert_eq!(cover.len(), 1);
        assert!(cover.contains(&Vertex(1)));
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_min_vertex_cover_triangle_graph() {
        // Graph: 0--1, 1--2, 2--0
        let mut graph = Graph::new(3);
        graph.add_edge(0, 1);
        graph.add_edge(1, 2);
        graph.add_edge(2, 0);
        let cover = graph.min_vertex_cover();
        assert_eq!(cover.len(), 2);
        // Possible covers: {0,1}, {1,2}, {0,2}
        let expected1: HashSet<Vertex> = [Vertex(0), Vertex(1)].iter().cloned().collect();
        let expected2: HashSet<Vertex> = [Vertex(1), Vertex(2)].iter().cloned().collect();
        let expected3: HashSet<Vertex> = [Vertex(0), Vertex(2)].iter().cloned().collect();
        assert!(cover == expected1 || cover == expected2 || cover == expected3);
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_min_vertex_cover_star_graph() {
        // Star graph: 0 is center, connected to 1, 2, 3
        let mut graph = Graph::new(4);
        graph.add_edge(0, 1);
        graph.add_edge(0, 2);
        graph.add_edge(0, 3);
        let cover = graph.min_vertex_cover();
        assert_eq!(cover.len(), 1);
        assert!(cover.contains(&Vertex(0)));
    }

    // A more complex graph, often used for testing MVC
    // 0--1--2
    // |  |  |
    // 3--4--5
    #[test]
    fn test_min_vertex_cover_grid_graph() {
        let mut graph = Graph::new(6);
        graph.add_edge(0, 1);
        graph.add_edge(1, 2);
        graph.add_edge(0, 3);
        graph.add_edge(1, 4);
        graph.add_edge(2, 5);
        graph.add_edge(3, 4);
        graph.add_edge(4, 5);

        let cover = graph.min_vertex_cover();
        // The minimum vertex cover for this graph is 3.
        // Example covers: {1,3,5}, {0,2,4}, {0,1,5}, {0,2,3}, etc.
        assert_eq!(cover.len(), 3);
        // We cannot assert specific vertices easily because multiple valid MVCs exist.
        // Instead, we verify that the size is correct and that it actually is a vertex cover.
        assert!(is_vertex_cover(&graph, &cover));
    }

    // Helper function to check if a given set of vertices is a valid vertex cover
    fn is_vertex_cover(graph: &Graph, cover: &HashSet<Vertex>) -> bool {
        for u in 0..graph.num_vertices {
            for v in graph.adj[&Vertex(u)].iter() {
                if u < v.0 { // Consider each edge only once
                    if !cover.contains(&Vertex(u)) && !cover.contains(v) {
                        return false; // Edge (u,v) is not covered
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        true
    }
}

using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;
using System.Linq;

namespace MaximumCliqueSolver
{
    // Represents a graph using an adjacency list
    public class Graph
    {
        private readonly int _numVertices;
        private readonly HashSet<int>[] _adj;

        public Graph(int numVertices)
        {
            _numVertices = numVertices;
            _adj = new HashSet<int>[numVertices];
            for (int i = 0; i < numVertices; i++)
            {
                _adj[i] = new HashSet<int>();
            }
        }

        // Add an edge between two vertices
        public void AddEdge(int u, int v)
        {
            _adj[u].Add(v);
            _adj[v].Add(u); // Assuming undirected graph
        }

        // Get neighbors of a vertex
        public HashSet<int> GetNeighbors(int v)
        {
            return _adj[v];
        }

        // Check if two vertices are adjacent
        public bool AreAdjacent(int u, int v)
        {
            return _adj[u].Contains(v);
        }

        public int NumVertices => _numVertices;
    }

    // Solves the Maximum Clique problem using a backtracking approach (Bron-Kerbosch-like)
    public class MaximumCliqueSolver
    {
        private Graph _graph;
        private List<int> _maxClique;

        public MaximumCliqueSolver(Graph graph)
        {
            _graph = graph;
            _maxClique = new List<int>();
        }

        public List<int> FindMaximumClique()
        {
            _maxClique.Clear();
            List<int> currentClique = new List<int>();
            HashSet<int> candidates = new HashSet<int>(Enumerable.Range(0, _graph.NumVertices));

            BronKerbosch(currentClique, candidates, new HashSet<int>());

            return _maxClique;
        }

        private void BronKerbosch(List<int> R, HashSet<int> P, HashSet<int> X)
        {
            if (P.Count == 0 && X.Count == 0)
            {
                if (R.Count > _maxClique.Count)
                {
                    _maxClique = new List<int>(R);
                }
                return;
            }

            int pivot = -1;
            int maxDegree = -1;
            // Combine P and X for pivot selection
            var P_union_X = P.Union(X); 

            foreach (int v in P_union_X)
            {
                int degree = _graph.GetNeighbors(v).Intersect(P).Count(); 
                if (degree > maxDegree)
                {
                    maxDegree = degree;
                    pivot = v;
                }
            }

            // P_minus_N_pivot = P \ N(pivot)
            // Iterate over a copy to allow modification of P inside the loop
            var P_minus_N_pivot_list = P.Except(_graph.GetNeighbors(pivot)).ToList();

            foreach (int v in P_minus_N_pivot_list)
            {
                R.Add(v);
                var N_v = _graph.GetNeighbors(v);
                
                // Create new HashSets for the recursive call to maintain state for backtracking
                BronKerbosch(R, new HashSet<int>(P.Intersect(N_v)), new HashSet<int>(X.Union(new HashSet<int> { v }).Intersect(N_v)));
                
                R.Remove(v);
                P.Remove(v); // Remove v from candidates as well for the current level of recursion
                X.Add(v); // Add v to the excluded set for the current level of recursion
            }
        }
    }

    class Program
    {
        static void Main(string[] args)
        {
            string line = Console.ReadLine();
            string[] parts = line.Split(' ');
            int numVertices = int.Parse(parts[0]);
            int numEdges = int.Parse(parts[1]);

            Graph graph = new Graph(numVertices);

            for (int i = 0; i < numEdges; i++)
            {
                line = Console.ReadLine();
                parts = line.Split(' ');
                int u = int.Parse(parts[0]);
                int v = int.Parse(parts[1]);
                graph.AddEdge(u, v);
            }

            MaximumCliqueSolver solver = new MaximumCliqueSolver(graph);
            List<int> maxClique = solver.FindMaximumClique();

            Console.WriteLine(maxClique.Count);
            Console.WriteLine(string.Join(" ", maxClique));
        }
    }
}

using System.Collections.Generic;
using System.Linq;

namespace MaximumCliqueSolver
{
    // Represents a graph using an adjacency list
    public class Graph
    {
        private readonly int _numVertices;
        private readonly HashSet<int>[] _adj;

        public Graph(int numVertices)
        {
            _numVertices = numVertices;
            _adj = new HashSet<int>[numVertices];
            for (int i = 0; i < numVertices; i++)
            {
                _adj[i] = new HashSet<int>();
            }
        }

        // Add an edge between two vertices
        public void AddEdge(int u, int v)
        {
            _adj[u].Add(v);
            _adj[v].Add(u); // Assuming undirected graph
        }

        // Get neighbors of a vertex
        public HashSet<int> GetNeighbors(int v)
        {
            return _adj[v];
        }

        // Check if two vertices are adjacent
        public bool AreAdjacent(int u, int v)
        {
            return _adj[u].Contains(v);
        }

        public int NumVertices => _numVertices;
    }

    // Solves the Maximum Clique problem using a backtracking approach (Bron-Kerbosch-like)
    public class MaximumCliqueSolver
    {
        private Graph _graph;
        private List<int> _maxClique;

        public MaximumCliqueSolver(Graph graph)
        {
            _graph = graph;
            _maxClique = new List<int>();
        }

        public List<int> FindMaximumClique()
        {
            _maxClique.Clear();
            List<int> currentClique = new List<int>();
            HashSet<int> candidates = new HashSet<int>(Enumerable.Range(0, _graph.NumVertices));

            BronKerbosch(currentClique, candidates, new HashSet<int>());

            return _maxClique;
        }

        private void BronKerbosch(List<int> R, HashSet<int> P, HashSet<int> X)
        {
            if (P.Count == 0 && X.Count == 0)
            {
                if (R.Count > _maxClique.Count)
                {
                    _maxClique = new List<int>(R);
                }
                return;
            }

            int pivot = -1;
            int maxDegree = -1;

            var P_union_X = P.Union(X);

            {
                int degree = _graph.GetNeighbors(v).Intersect(P).Count(); 
                if (degree > maxDegree)
                {
                    maxDegree = degree;
                    pivot = v;
                }
            }

            // P_minus_N_pivot = P \ N(pivot)
            // Iterate over a copy to allow modification of P inside the loop
            var P_minus_N_pivot_list = P.Except(_graph.GetNeighbors(pivot)).ToList();

            foreach (int v in P_minus_N_pivot_list)
            {
                R.Add(v);
                var N_v = _graph.GetNeighbors(v);
                
                // Create new HashSets for the recursive call to maintain state for backtracking
                BronKerbosch(R, new HashSet<int>(P.Intersect(N_v)), new HashSet<int>(X.Union(new HashSet<int> { v }).Intersect(N_v)));
                
                R.Remove(v);
                P.Remove(v); // Remove v from candidates as well for the current level of recursion
                X.Add(v); // Add v to the excluded set for the current level of recursion
            }
        }
    }

    class Program
    {
        static void Main(string[] args)
        {
            string line = Console.ReadLine();

            HashSet<int> candidates = new HashSet<int>(Enumerable.Range(0, _graph.NumVertices));

            BronKerbosch(currentClique, candidates, new HashSet<int>());

            return _maxClique;
        }

        private void BronKerbosch(List<int> R, HashSet<int> P, HashSet<int> X)
        {
            if (P.Count == 0 && X.Count == 0)
            {
                if (R.Count > _maxClique.Count)
                {
                    _maxClique = new List<int>(R);
                }
                return;
            }

            int pivot = -1;
            int maxDegree = -1;
            // Combine P and X for pivot selection
            var P_union_X = P.Union(X); 

            foreach (int v in P_union_X)
            {
                int degree = _graph.GetNeighbors(v).Intersect(P).Count(); 
                if (degree > maxDegree)
                {
                    maxDegree = degree;
                    pivot = v;
                }
            }

            // P_minus_N_pivot = P \ N(pivot)
            // Iterate over a copy to allow modification of P inside the loop
            var P_minus_N_pivot_list = P.Except(_graph.GetNeighbors(pivot)).ToList();

            foreach (int v in P_minus_N_pivot_list)
            {
                R.Add(v);
                var N_v = _graph.GetNeighbors(v);
                
                // Create new HashSets for the recursive call to maintain state for backtracking
                BronKerbosch(R, new HashSet<int>(P.Intersect(N_v)), new HashSet<int>(X.Union(new HashSet<int> { v }).Intersect(N_v)));
                
                R.Remove(v);
                P.Remove(v); // Remove v from candidates as well for the current level of recursion
                X.Add(v); // Add v to the excluded set for the current level of recursion
            }
        }
    }

    class Program
    {
        static void Main(string[] args)
        {
            string line = Console.ReadLine();
            string[] parts = line.Split(' ');
            int numVertices = int.Parse(parts[0]);
            int numEdges = int.Parse(parts[1]);

            Graph graph = new Graph(numVertices);

            for (int i = 0; i < numEdges; i++)
            {
                line = Console.ReadLine();
                parts = line.Split(' ');
                int u = int.Parse(parts[0]);
                int v = int.Parse(parts[1]);
                graph.AddEdge(u, v);
            }

            MaximumCliqueSolver solver = new MaximumCliqueSolver(graph);
            List<int> maxClique = solver.FindMaximumClique();

            Console.WriteLine(maxClique.Count);
            Console.WriteLine(string.Join(" ", maxClique));
        }
    }
}

Typical Prompt:
You are writing Python code to solve the 3-SAT (Boolean Satisfiability) problem, which is NP-Complete.

**What is 3-SAT?**
You have N boolean variables (x1, x2, ..., xN), each of which is either True or False.
You are given M "clauses". Each clause is a constraint containing exactly 3 "literals".
A literal is either:
- A positive integer (e.g. 5) meaning "variable 5 must be True", or
- A negative integer (e.g. -5) meaning "variable 5 must be False".

A clause is **satisfied** if ANY of its 3 literals evaluates to True.
The formula is **satisfiable** if ALL clauses can be satisfied simultaneously
by some assignment of True/False to the variables.

**Example:**
Variables: x1, x2, x3
Clause "1 -2 3" means: x1=True OR x2=False OR x3=True.
If x1=True, x2=True, x3=False → clause satisfied (x1=True is enough).

Your task: find an assignment of True/False to every variable that satisfies
every clause. All test instances are guaranteed to be satisfiable.

**Input format (stdin):**
```
num_variables num_clauses
lit1 lit2 lit3
lit1 lit2 lit3
...
```
Variables are 1-indexed. Negative literals mean negation.

**Output format (stdout):**
```
SAT
v1 v2 v3 ... vN
```
Where each vi is 1 (True) or 0 (False) for variable i, space-separated.

**Grading:**
- Output "SAT" on the first line, then the assignment on the second line.
- Every clause must be satisfied by your assignment.
- Timeouts, crashes, wrong format, or unsatisfied clauses all score 0.

**Requirements:**
1. Read from stdin, write to stdout.
2. Handle up to 20M variables and 85M clauses.
3. Complete within 5 minutes.

import sys
import random
import time

def solve_3sat():
    start_time = time.time()

    # Read num_variables and num_clauses
    line = sys.stdin.readline().split()
    num_variables = int(line[0])
    num_clauses = int(line[1])

    clauses = []
    for _ in range(num_clauses):
        clause_literals = list(map(int, sys.stdin.readline().split()))
        clauses.append(clause_literals)

    # Initialize a random assignment
    # Using a list where index i corresponds to variable i+1
    # value is 0 for False, 1 for True
    current_assignment = [random.randint(0, 1) for _ in range(num_variables)]

    # --- Local Search Algorithm ---
    max_flips = 10 * num_variables  # Heuristic for max iterations
    max_tries = 5 # Number of random restarts

    for _try in range(max_tries):
        # Reset assignment for each try
        current_assignment = [random.randint(0, 1) for _ in range(num_variables)]

        for _flip in range(max_flips):
            # Check if current assignment satisfies all clauses
            satisfied_all = True
            unsatisfied_clauses_indices = []

            for i, clause in enumerate(clauses):
                clause_satisfied = False
                for literal in clause:
                    var_index = abs(literal) - 1
                    var_value = current_assignment[var_index]
                    
                    if (literal > 0 and var_value == 1) or 
                       (literal < 0 and var_value == 0):
                        clause_satisfied = True
                        break
                
                if not clause_satisfied:
                    satisfied_all = False
                    unsatisfied_clauses_indices.append(i)
            
            if satisfied_all:
                print("SAT")
                print(*(1 if val else 0 for val in current_assignment))
                return

            # Pick a random unsatisfied clause
            if not unsatisfied_clauses_indices: # Should not happen if not satisfied_all is True
                continue

            target_clause_index = random.choice(unsatisfied_clauses_indices)
            target_clause = clauses[target_clause_index]

            # Decide which literal's variable to flip
            # Simplified approach: randomly pick one of the literals in the clause
            literal_to_flip = random.choice(target_clause)
            var_to_flip_index = abs(literal_to_flip) - 1
            
            current_assignment[var_to_flip_index] = 1 - current_assignment[var_to_flip_index] # Flip the variable

    # If after all tries and flips, no solution is found (shouldn't happen based on problem statement)
    sys.stderr.write("No solution found within limits (problem guarantees satisfiability).
")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    solve_3sat()

fn subset_sum(nums: &[i32], target: i32) -> bool {
    let n = nums.len();
    let mut dp = vec![vec![false; (target + 1) as usize]; n + 1];

    // Base case: if target is 0, an empty subset sums to 0
    for i in 0..=n {
        dp[i][0] = true;
    }

    // Fill the dp table
    for i in 1..=n {
        for j in 1..=target {
            // If the current number is greater than the current sum,
            // we cannot include it. So, the result is the same as
            // without the current number.
            if nums[i - 1] > j {
                dp[i][j] = dp[i - 1][j];
            } else {
                // If we include the current number, check if the remaining
                // sum (j - nums[i-1]) can be formed by previous numbers.
                // Or, if we don't include the current number, check if
                // the current sum (j) can be formed by previous numbers.
                dp[i][j] = dp[i - 1][j] || dp[i - 1][(j - nums[i - 1]) as usize];
            }
        }
    }

    dp[n][target as usize]
}

fn main() {
    // Test cases
    let nums1 = vec![3, 34, 4, 12, 5, 2];
    let target1 = 9;
    println!("Can subset_sum({:?}, {}) be formed? {}", nums1, target1, subset_sum(&nums1, target1)); // Expected: true (4 + 5)

    let nums2 = vec![3, 34, 4, 12, 5, 2];
    let target2 = 30;
    println!("Can subset_sum({:?}, {}) be formed? {}", nums2, target2, subset_sum(&nums2, target2)); // Expected: false

    let nums3 = vec![1, 2, 3];
    let target3 = 6;
    println!("Can subset_sum({:?}, {}) be formed? {}", nums3, target3, subset_sum(&nums3, target3)); // Expected: true (1 + 2 + 3)

    let nums4 = vec![1, 2, 3];
    let target4 = 7;
    println!("Can subset_sum({:?}, {}) be formed? {}", nums4, target4, subset_sum(&nums4, target4)); // Expected: false

    let nums5 = vec![];
    let target5 = 0;
    println!("Can subset_sum({:?}, {}) be formed? {}", nums5, target5, subset_sum(&nums5, target5)); // Expected: true

    let nums6 = vec![10];
    let target6 = 10;
    println!("Can subset_sum({:?}, {}) be formed? {}", nums6, target6, subset_sum(&nums6, target6)); // Expected: true

    let nums7 = vec![10];
    let target7 = 5;
    println!("Can subset_sum({:?}, {}) be formed? {}", nums7, target7, subset_sum(&nums7, target7)); // Expected: false

#include "steiner_tree.h"
#include <algorithm> // For std::min
#include <map>

SteinerTreeSolver::SteinerTreeSolver(int num_vertices)
    : num_vertices_(num_vertices),
      adj_(num_vertices),
      dist_(num_vertices, std::vector<int>(num_vertices, INF)) {
    for (int i = 0; i < num_vertices_; ++i) {
        dist_[i][i] = 0;
    }
}

void SteinerTreeSolver::add_edge(int u, int v, int weight) {
    adj_[u].push_back({v, weight});
    adj_[v].push_back({u, weight});
    dist_[u][v] = std::min(dist_[u][v], weight);
    dist_[v][u] = std::min(dist_[v][u], weight);
}

void SteinerTreeSolver::set_terminals(const std::vector<int>& terminals) {
    terminals_ = terminals;
    terminal_to_idx_.clear();
    for (int i = 0; i < terminals_.size(); ++i) {
        terminal_to_idx_[terminals_[i]] = i;
    }
}

void SteinerTreeSolver::compute_all_pairs_shortest_paths() {
    // Initialize dist_ with direct edge weights and INF for no direct edge
    // This is already done in add_edge for direct connections and constructor for self-loops.
    // For non-existent direct edges, dist_ is already INF.

    // Floyd-Warshall algorithm
    for (int k = 0; k < num_vertices_; ++k) {
        for (int i = 0; i < num_vertices_; ++i) {
            for (int j = 0; j < num_vertices_; ++j) {
                if (dist_[i][k] != INF && dist_[k][j] != INF) {
                    dist_[i][j] = std::min(dist_[i][j], dist_[i][k] + dist_[k][j]);
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

int SteinerTreeSolver::solve() {
    // This will be implemented in subsequent steps.
    // For now, call APSP to ensure it's computed.
    compute_all_pairs_shortest_paths();
    return calculate_steiner_tree_cost(); // Placeholder
}

int SteinerTreeSolver::calculate_steiner_tree_cost() {
    int num_terminals = terminals_.size();
    if (num_terminals == 0) {
        return 0; // No terminals, cost is 0
    }
    if (num_vertices_ == 0) {
        return INF; // No vertices, cannot form a tree
    }

    // dp[mask][v] = minimum cost of a Steiner tree connecting terminals in mask,
    // where vertex v is part of the tree.
    // The mask represents a subset of terminals.
    std::vector<std::vector<int>> dp(1 << num_terminals, std::vector<int>(num_vertices_, INF));

    // Initialization: Base cases for DP
    // For each terminal, a tree containing only itself has cost 0.
    for (int i = 0; i < num_terminals; ++i) {
        dp[1 << i][terminals_[i]] = 0;
    }

    // DP Iteration
    // Iterate over increasing mask values (subsets of terminals)
    for (int mask = 1; mask < (1 << num_terminals); ++mask) {
        // Case 1: Merging Subtrees (connecting two smaller Steiner trees)
        // Try all possible splits of 'mask' into 'submask' and 'mask ^ submask'
        for (int submask = (mask - 1) & mask; submask > 0; submask = (submask - 1) & mask) {
            int remaining_mask = mask ^ submask;
            for (int v = 0; v < num_vertices_; ++v) {
                if (dp[submask][v] != INF && dp[remaining_mask][v] != INF) {
                    dp[mask][v] = std::min(dp[mask][v], dp[submask][v] + dp[remaining_mask][v]);
                }
            }
        }

        // Case 2: Shortest Path Connection (extending a subtree from u to v)
        // This is like running Dijkstra for each mask.
        // Relax edges using all-pairs shortest paths (dist_)
        // We iterate k times to simulate shortest path finding for current mask
        // This is effectively a Bellman-Ford like relaxation for the current mask.
        // A more efficient way would be to use a priority queue for each mask,
        // but for simplicity and within limits of this problem size, this can work.
        // For each mask, ensure that the minimum cost to reach 'v' from any 'u'
        // that is already part of the subtree 'mask' is considered.
        // This part means that we try to improve dp[mask][v] by connecting it to dp[mask][u]
        // via shortest path dist[u][v].
        bool changed;
        for (int iter = 0; iter < num_vertices_; ++iter) { // iterate V times for Bellman-Ford style relaxation
            changed = false;
            for (int v = 0; v < num_vertices_; ++v) {
                for (int u = 0; u < num_vertices_; ++u) {
                    if (dp[mask][u] != INF && dist_[u][v] != INF) {
                        if (dp[mask][v] > dp[mask][u] + dist_[u][v]) {
                            dp[mask][v] = dp[mask][u] + dist_[u][v];
                            changed = true;
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
            if (!changed) {
                break;
            }
        }
    }

    // Final Result: Find the minimum cost for the tree connecting all terminals.
    int min_steiner_tree_cost = INF;
    int all_terminals_mask = (1 << num_terminals) - 1;
    for (int v = 0; v < num_vertices_; ++v) {
        min_steiner_tree_cost = std::min(min_steiner_tree_cost, dp[all_terminals_mask][v]);
    }

    return min_steiner_tree_cost;
}

#include "steiner_tree.h"
#include <algorithm> // For std::min
#include <map>

SteinerTreeSolver::SteinerTreeSolver(int num_vertices)
    : num_vertices_(num_vertices),
      adj_(num_vertices),
      dist_(num_vertices, std::vector<int>(num_vertices, INF)) {
    for (int i = 0; i < num_vertices_; ++i) {
        dist_[i][i] = 0;
    }
}

void SteinerTreeSolver::add_edge(int u, int v, int weight) {
    adj_[u].push_back({v, weight});
    adj_[v].push_back({u, weight});
    dist_[u][v] = std::min(dist_[u][v], weight);
    dist_[v][u] = std::min(dist_[v][u], weight);
}

void SteinerTreeSolver::set_terminals(const std::vector<int>& terminals) {
    terminals_ = terminals;
    terminal_to_idx_.clear();
    for (int i = 0; i < terminals_.size(); ++i) {
        terminal_to_idx_[terminals_[i]] = i;
    }
}

void SteinerTreeSolver::compute_all_pairs_shortest_paths() {
    // Initialize dist_ with direct edge weights and INF for no direct edge
    // This is already done in add_edge for direct connections and constructor for self-loops.
    // For non-existent direct edges, dist_ is already INF.

    // Floyd-Warshall algorithm
    for (int k = 0; k < num_vertices_; ++k) {
        for (int i = 0; i < num_vertices_; ++i) {
            for (int j = 0; j < num_vertices_; ++j) {
                if (dist_[i][k] != INF && dist_[k][j] != INF) {
                    dist_[i][j] = std::min(dist_[i][j], dist_[i][k] + dist_[k][j]);
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

int SteinerTreeSolver::solve() {

    // For now, call APSP to ensure it's computed.
    compute_all_pairs_shortest_paths();
    return calculate_steiner_tree_cost(); // Placeholder
}

int SteinerTreeSolver::calculate_steiner_tree_cost() {
    int num_terminals = terminals_.size();
    if (num_terminals == 0) {
        return 0; // No terminals, cost is 0
    }
    if (num_vertices_ == 0) {
        return INF; // No vertices, cannot form a tree
    }

    // dp[mask][v] = minimum cost of a Steiner tree connecting terminals in mask,
    // where vertex v is part of the tree.
    // The mask represents a subset of terminals.
    std::vector<std::vector<int>> dp(1 << num_terminals, std::vector<int>(num_vertices_, INF));

    // Initialization: Base cases for DP
    // For each terminal, a tree containing only itself has cost 0.
    for (int i = 0; i < num_terminals; ++i) {
        dp[1 << i][terminals_[i]] = 0;
    }

    // DP Iteration
    // Iterate over increasing mask values (subsets of terminals)
    for (int mask = 1; mask < (1 << num_terminals); ++mask) {
        // Case 1: Merging Subtrees (connecting two smaller Steiner trees)
        // Try all possible splits of 'mask' into 'submask' and 'mask ^ submask'
        for (int submask = (mask - 1) & mask; submask > 0; submask = (submask - 1) & mask) {
            int remaining_mask = mask ^ submask;
            for (int v = 0; v < num_vertices_; ++v) {
                if (dp[submask][v] != INF && dp[remaining_mask][v] != INF) {
                    dp[mask][v] = std::min(dp[mask][v], dp[submask][v] + dp[remaining_mask][v]);
                }
            }
        }

        // Case 2: Shortest Path Connection (extending a subtree from u to v)
        // This is like running Dijkstra for each mask.
        // Relax edges using all-pairs shortest paths (dist_)
        // We iterate k times to simulate shortest path finding for current mask
        // This is effectively a Bellman-Ford like relaxation for the current mask.
        // A more efficient way would be to use a priority queue for each mask,
        // but for simplicity and within limits of this problem size, this can work.
        // For each mask, ensure that the minimum cost to reach 'v' from any 'u'
        // that is already part of the subtree 'mask' is considered.
        // This part means that we try to improve dp[mask][v] by connecting it to dp[mask][u]
        // via shortest path dist[u][v].
        bool changed;
        for (int iter = 0; iter < num_vertices_; ++iter) { // iterate V times for Bellman-Ford style relaxation
            changed = false;
            for (int v = 0; v < num_vertices_; ++v) {
                for (int u = 0; u < num_vertices_; ++u) {
                    if (dp[mask][u] != INF && dist_[u][v] != INF) {
                        if (dp[mask][v] > dp[mask][u] + dist_[u][v]) {
                            dp[mask][v] = dp[mask][u] + dist_[u][v];
                            changed = true;
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
            if (!changed) {
                break;
            }
        }
    }

    // Final Result: Find the minimum cost for the tree connecting all terminals.
    int min_steiner_tree_cost = INF;
    int all_terminals_mask = (1 << num_terminals) - 1;
    for (int v = 0; v < num_vertices_; ++v) {
        min_steiner_tree_cost = std::min(min_steiner_tree_cost, dp[all_terminals_mask][v]);
    }

    return min_steiner_tree_cost;
}

**Problem:**

sum over all pairs (i, j): flow[i][j] * distance[p[i]][p[j]]

Your goal is to minimize this total cost.

**Input format (stdin):**
```
N
flow[0][0] flow[0][1] ... flow[0][N-1]
...

...

```
All values are integers. Matrices are N×N. Indices are 0-based in the output.

**Output format (stdout):**
```
total_cost
p0 p1 p2 ... p(N-1)
```
Where p is a permutation of 0..N-1 and p[i] is the location assigned to facility i.

**Requirements:**
1. Read from stdin, write to stdout.
2. Output a valid permutation.
3. Handle N from very small up to ~2000 within 5 minutes.
4. Heuristics are acceptable for large N; lower cost scores higher.

using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;
using System.Linq;

public class Program
{
    public static void Main(string[] args)
    {
        // Read input
        int n = int.Parse(Console.ReadLine());

        int[][] flow = ReadMatrix(n);
        int[][] dist = ReadMatrix(n);

        // Initialize a random permutation
        int[] bestPermutation = Enumerable.Range(0, n).ToArray();
        Shuffle(bestPermutation); // Random initial permutation

        long bestCost = CalculateCost(bestPermutation, flow, dist);

        // --- Simulated Annealing Algorithm ---
        // Parameters (can be tuned)
        double temperature = 100000.0;
        double coolingRate = 0.999; // Adjust based on N
        int maxIterations = 1000000; // Adjust based on N

        Random rand = new Random();

        for (int i = 0; i < maxIterations; i++)
        {
            if (temperature <= 0.1) break; // Stop if temperature is too low

            // Generate a neighbor solution by swapping two elements
            int[] currentPermutation = (int[])bestPermutation.Clone();
            int idx1 = rand.Next(n);
            int idx2 = rand.Next(n);
            while (idx1 == idx2)
            {
                idx2 = rand.Next(n);
            }
            Swap(currentPermutation, idx1, idx2);

            long currentCost = CalculateCost(currentPermutation, flow, dist);

            // Decide whether to accept the new solution
            if (currentCost < bestCost)
            {
                bestCost = currentCost;
                bestPermutation = currentPermutation;
            }
            else if (AcceptanceProbability(bestCost, currentCost, temperature, rand) > rand.NextDouble())
            {
                bestCost = currentCost;
                bestPermutation = currentPermutation;
            }

            temperature *= coolingRate; // Cool down
        }

        // Output result
        Console.WriteLine(bestCost);
        Console.WriteLine(string.Join(" ", bestPermutation));
    }

    // Reads an N x N matrix from console input
    private static int[][] ReadMatrix(int n)
    {
        int[][] matrix = new int[n][];
        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)
        {
            matrix[i] = Console.ReadLine().Split(' ').Select(int.Parse).ToArray();
        }
        return matrix;
    }

    // Calculates the cost of a given permutation
    private static long CalculateCost(int[] permutation, int[][] flow, int[][] dist)
    {
        long cost = 0;
        int n = permutation.Length;
        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)
        {
            for (int j = 0; j < n; j++)
            {
                cost += (long)flow[i][j] * dist[permutation[i]][permutation[j]];
            }
        }
        return cost;
    }

    // Shuffles an array (Fisher-Yates)
    private static void Shuffle<T>(T[] array)
    {
        Random rand = new Random();
        int n = array.Length;
        for (int i = n - 1; i > 0; i--)
        {
            int j = rand.Next(i + 1);
            Swap(array, i, j);
        }
    }

    // Swaps two elements in an array
    private static void Swap<T>(T[] array, int i, int j)
    {
        T temp = array[i];
        array[i] = array[j];
        array[j] = temp;
    }

    // Calculates the acceptance probability for Simulated Annealing
    private static double AcceptanceProbability(long energy, long newEnergy, double temperature, Random rand)
    {
        if (newEnergy < energy)
        {
            return 1.0;
        }
        return Math.Exp((energy - newEnergy) / temperature);
    }
}

import math
import sys

class Customer:
    def __init__(self, id, x, y, demand):
        self.id = id
        self.x = x
        self.y = y
        self.demand = demand

class Depot:
    def __init__(self, x, y):
        self.x = x
        self.y = y

def calculate_distance(p1_x, p1_y, p2_x, p2_y):
    return math.sqrt((p1_x - p2_x)**2 + (p1_y - p2_y)**2)

def parse_input():
    lines = sys.stdin.readlines()
    
    # N K CAPACITY
    n, k, capacity = map(int, lines[0].split())

    # depot_x depot_y
    depot_x, depot_y = map(int, lines[1].split())
    depot = Depot(depot_x, depot_y)

    customers = []
    for i in range(2, 2 + n):
        parts = list(map(int, lines[i].split()))
        customers.append(Customer(i - 2, parts[0], parts[1], parts[2])) # 0-based index

    return n, k, capacity, depot, customers

def solve_cvrp(n, k, capacity, depot, customers):
    unvisited_customers = set(customer.id for customer in customers)
    routes = []
    total_overall_distance = 0.0

    customer_map = {customer.id: customer for customer in customers}

    while unvisited_customers:
        if len(routes) >= k: # If we exceed the maximum number of routes, we might have an issue
            # This case indicates that even with k vehicles, we can't serve all customers
            # With Nearest Neighbor, this usually means capacity or k is too restrictive.
            # For now, we'll proceed, but a more robust solution might handle this differently.
            pass

        current_route = []
        current_load = 0
        current_x, current_y = depot.x, depot.y
        route_distance = 0.0

        # Start a new route
        while True:
            nearest_customer_id = -1
            min_distance = float('inf')

            for customer_id in unvisited_customers:
                customer = customer_map[customer_id]
                if current_load + customer.demand <= capacity:
                    dist = calculate_distance(current_x, current_y, customer.x, customer.y)
                    if dist < min_distance:
                        min_distance = dist
                        nearest_customer_id = customer_id
            
            if nearest_customer_id != -1:
                customer = customer_map[nearest_customer_id]
                current_route.append(nearest_customer_id)
                unvisited_customers.remove(nearest_customer_id)
                current_load += customer.demand
                route_distance += min_distance
                current_x, current_y = customer.x, customer.y
            else:
                # No more customers can be added to this route (either all visited or capacity reached)
                break
        
        if not current_route and unvisited_customers: # This can happen if a single customer's demand exceeds capacity
            # Or if k is too small to cover all customers
            # For this simple Nearest Neighbor, it means a customer cannot be served by any vehicle due to capacity.
            # A more advanced algorithm would handle this (e.g., by relaxing capacity or assigning large demand customers specially).
            # For now, we assume valid input where this won't be an issue based on problem statement.
            break # Exit if no customers could be added but some are still unvisited

        if current_route: # If the route is not empty, add return trip to depot
            route_distance += calculate_distance(current_x, current_y, depot.x, depot.y)
            routes.append(current_route)
            total_overall_distance += route_distance

        if not unvisited_customers:
            break # All customers visited

    return total_overall_distance, len(routes), routes

def main():
    n, k, capacity, depot, customers = parse_input()
    total_distance, num_routes, routes = solve_cvrp(n, k, capacity, depot, customers)

    print(f"{total_distance}")
    print(f"{num_routes}")
    for route in routes:
        print(" ".join(map(str, route)))

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

            min_distance = float('inf')

            for customer_id in unvisited_customers:
                customer = customer_map[customer_id]
                if current_load + customer.demand <= capacity:
                    dist = calculate_distance(current_x, current_y, customer.x, customer.y)
                    if dist < min_distance:
                        min_distance = dist
                        nearest_customer_id = customer_id
            
            if nearest_customer_id != -1:
                customer = customer_map[nearest_customer_id]
                current_route.append(nearest_customer_id)
                unvisited_customers.remove(nearest_customer_id)
                current_load += customer.demand
                route_distance += min_distance
                current_x, current_y = customer.x, customer.y
            else:
                # No more customers can be added to this route (either all visited or capacity reached)
                break
        
        if not current_route and unvisited_customers: # This can happen if a single customer's demand exceeds capacity
            # Or if k is too small to cover all customers
            # For this simple Nearest Neighbor, it means a customer cannot be served by any vehicle due to capacity.
            # A more advanced algorithm would handle this (e.g., by relaxing capacity or assigning large demand customers specially).
            # For now, we assume valid input where this won't be an issue based on problem statement.
            break # Exit if no customers could be added but some are still unvisited

        if current_route: # If the route is not empty, add return trip to depot
            route_distance += calculate_distance(current_x, current_y, depot.x, depot.y)
            routes.append(current_route)
            total_overall_distance += route_distance

        if not unvisited_customers:
            break # All customers visited

    return total_overall_distance, len(routes), routes

def main():
    n, k, capacity, depot, customers = parse_input()
    total_distance, num_routes, routes = solve_cvrp(n, k, capacity, depot, customers)

    print(f"{total_distance}")
    print(f"{num_routes}")
    for route in routes:
        print(" ".join(map(str, route)))

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
