import * as fs from 'fs';

interface Town {
    id: string;
    x: number;
    y: number;
    value: number;
}

interface InputData {
    width: number;
    height: number;
    grid: string[];
    ignitions: [number, number][];
    towns: Town[];
    cutBudget: number;
}

interface OutputData {
    firebreaks: [number, number][];
}

const input: string = fs.readFileSync(0, 'utf8');
const data: InputData = JSON.parse(input);

function solve(): OutputData {
    const { width, height, grid, ignitions, towns, cutBudget } = data;

    // Grid representation: 0 = forest, 1 = water/rock, 2 = cut firebreak
    const initialGrid: number[][] = Array.from({ length: height }, (_, y) =>
        Array.from({ length: width }, (_, x) => (grid[y][x] === '.' ? 0 : 1))
    );

    // --- Step 1: Simulate fire without any firebreaks to determine baseline burned towns ---
    const burnedTownsWithoutFirebreaks = simulateFire(initialGrid, ignitions, towns, []);
    const totalBurnedValueWithoutFirebreaks = burnedTownsWithoutFirebreaks.reduce((sum, town) => sum + town.value, 0);

    // --- Step 2: Implement firebreak placement strategy ---
    // This is where the core algorithm will go. For now, a placeholder.

    // For a greedy approach, we could iterate, find the most impactful firebreak, add it, and repeat.
    // This will require re-simulating fire multiple times or a more advanced graph-based approach.

    let currentCuts = 0;
    for (let y = 0; y < height && currentCuts < cutBudget; y++) {
        for (let x = 0; x < width && currentCuts < cutBudget; x++) {
            if (initialGrid[y][x] === 0) { // If it's forest
                firebreaks.push([x, y]);
                currentCuts++;
            }
        }
    }
    */


    // --- Step 3: Simulate fire with chosen firebreaks to verify ---
    // (This step will be used for actual scoring/validation but not directly for choosing firebreaks in this solve function)
    // const gridWithFirebreaks = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(initialGrid)); // Deep copy
    // firebreaks.forEach(([x, y]) => {
    //     gridWithFirebreaks[y][x] = 2; // Mark as cut
    // });
    // const burnedTownsWithFirebreaks = simulateFire(gridWithFirebreaks, ignitions, towns, firebreaks);
    // const savedValue = totalBurnedValueWithoutFirebreaks - burnedTownsWithFirebreaks.reduce((sum, town) => sum + town.value, 0);


    return { firebreaks: firebreaks };
}

/**
 * Simulates fire spread on the grid and returns the list of towns that burned.
 * @param grid A 2D number array where 0=forest, 1=water/rock, 2=cut firebreak.
 * @param ignitions Starting fire cells.
 * @param allTowns List of all towns.
 * @param currentFirebreaks The firebreak cells currently applied to the grid (used to mark grid cells as 2)
 * @returns An array of towns that burned.
 */
function simulateFire(baseGrid: number[][], ignitions: [number, number][], allTowns: Town[], currentFirebreaks: [number, number][]): Town[] {
    const height = baseGrid.length;
    const width = baseGrid[0].length;

    // Create a mutable grid for simulation, applying firebreaks
    const simulationGrid: number[][] = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(baseGrid)); // Deep copy
    currentFirebreaks.forEach(([x, y]) => {
        if (y >= 0 && y < height && x >= 0 && x < width) {
            simulationGrid[y][x] = 2; // Mark as cut
        }
    });

    const fireQueue: [number, number][] = [];
    const burned: boolean[][] = Array.from({ length: height }, () =>
        Array.from({ length: width }, () => false)
    );

    // Initialize ignitions
    for (const [startX, startY] of ignitions) {
        if (startY >= 0 && startY < height && startX >= 0 && startX < width && simulationGrid[startY][startX] === 0 && !burned[startY][startX]) {
            fireQueue.push([startX, startY]);
            burned[startY][startX] = true;
        }
    }

    const dx = [-1, 1, 0, 0]; // Left, Right
    const dy = [0, 0, -1, 1]; // Up, Down

    let head = 0;
    while (head < fireQueue.length) {
        const [x, y] = fireQueue[head++];

        for (let i = 0; i < 4; i++) {
            const nx = x + dx[i];
            const ny = y + dy[i];

            // Check bounds and if it's a burnable, unburned forest cell
            if (
                ny >= 0 && ny < height &&
                nx >= 0 && nx < width &&
                simulationGrid[ny][nx] === 0 && // Is forest
                !burned[ny][nx]
            ) {
                burned[ny][nx] = true;
                fireQueue.push([nx, ny]);
            }
        }
    }

    const burnedTowns: Town[] = [];
    for (const town of allTowns) {
        if (town.y >= 0 && town.y < height && town.x >= 0 && town.x < width && burned[town.y][town.x]) {
            burnedTowns.push(town);
        }
    }

    return burnedTowns;
}


const result = solve();

/**
 * Calculates the nth Fibonacci number.
 * Uses an iterative approach to avoid recursion depth limits and improve performance.
 * @param n The index of the Fibonacci number to calculate (non-negative integer).
 * @returns The nth Fibonacci number.
 */
function fibonacci(n: number): number {
  if (n < 0) {
    throw new Error("Input cannot be negative.");
  }
  if (n === 0) {
    return 0;
  }
  if (n === 1) {
    return 1;
  }

  let a = 0;
  let b = 1;
  for (let i = 2; i <= n; i++) {
    const next = a + b;
    a = b;
    b = next;
  }
  return b;
}

function main() {
  const args = process.argv.slice(2);
  const nStr = args[0];

  if (!nStr) {
    console.error("Usage: ts-node src/index.ts <n>");
    process.exit(1);
  }

  const n = parseInt(nStr, 10);

  if (isNaN(n)) {
    console.error("Input must be a number.");
    process.exit(1);
  }

  try {
    const result = fibonacci(n);
    console.log(`The ${n}th Fibonacci number is: ${result}`);
  } catch (error: any) {
    console.error(`Error: ${error.message}`);
    process.exit(1);
  }
}

main();

interface Task {
    id: string;
    duration: number; // Time in minutes
    deps: string[]; // Array of task IDs that must complete before this task can start
    deadline: number; // Time in minutes from start of day
    weight: number; // Importance of the task
}

interface InputData {
    machineCount: number;
    tasks: Task[];
}

interface OutputOrder {
    order: string[]; // Array of task IDs in topological order
}

declare const require: any;
const fs = require('fs');
const input: string = fs.readFileSync(0, 'utf8');
const data: InputData = JSON.parse(input);

function topologicalSort(tasks: Task[]): string[] {
    const taskMap = new Map<string, Task>();
    for (const task of tasks) {
        taskMap.set(task.id, task);
    }

    const inDegree = new Map<string, number>();
    const adjList = new Map<string, string[]>(); // Graph where key depends on value

    for (const task of tasks) {
        inDegree.set(task.id, 0);
        adjList.set(task.id, []);
    }

    // Build graph and calculate in-degrees
    for (const task of tasks) {
        for (const depId of task.deps) {
            // depId -> task.id means task.id depends on depId
            // So, add task.id to the adjacency list of depId
            if (!adjList.has(depId)) {
                // This case handles a dependency that might not be in the tasks list
                // Although problem statement implies all deps are valid task IDs,
                // better to be safe or assume valid input
                // For now, let's assume all deps are valid task IDs present in 'tasks'
                // If not, this might cause issues or indicate malformed input.
                // For a benchmark, we assume valid inputs for simplicity.
                adjList.set(depId, []);
            }
            adjList.get(depId)?.push(task.id);
            inDegree.set(task.id, (inDegree.get(task.id) || 0) + 1);
        }
    }

    const queue: string[] = [];
    for (const task of tasks) {
        if (inDegree.get(task.id) === 0) {
            queue.push(task.id);
        }
    }

    const result: string[] = [];
    let head = 0; // Manual queue head for performance in Node.js array

    while (head < queue.length) {
        const uId = queue[head++];
        result.push(uId);

        for (const vId of adjList.get(uId) || []) {
            inDegree.set(vId, (inDegree.get(vId) || 0) - 1);
            if (inDegree.get(vId) === 0) {
                queue.push(vId);
            }
        }
    }

    // If there's a cycle, result.length will be less than tasks.length
    // The problem statement implies valid inputs, so we don't handle cycles explicitly.
    // If a cycle were present, this would be an invalid schedule.
    // For a benchmark, a valid topological sort is expected for valid inputs.
    return result;
}

const orderedTaskIds = topologicalSort(data.tasks);

const output: OutputOrder = {
    order: orderedTaskIds
};

console.log(JSON.stringify(output));
